bibliography.title: Ultrafast Lithium-Ion Transport Engineered by Nanoconfinement Effect

mechanism_relevant_findings: The enhanced ionic conductivity is attributed to the layer-by-layer cations and anions distribution induced by high surface charge and nanoconfinement effects in graphene oxide nanochannels.
In basic carbonate liquid electrolytes, the ion conduction behavior primarily relies on the vehicle transport model.
limitations: Little is known about the influence of complex organic solvent systems on nanoconfined Li-ion transport and its underlying transport mechanisms.

relevance_judgement.reason: The study provides insights into the mechanisms enhancing lithium-ion transport which is relevant to proton conduction research.
